attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post. He is relaying FT reporting, but he states the score himself and stands behind it.

semantics.note: The normalised claim keeps the player, his amateur status, the top-AI opponent and the 14–1 score in 15 games. It is a past-tense factual observation.

contract.note: Reading 'top' as a leading system in ordinary play is the ordinary reading and fair to Marcus. The support and contradiction conditions follow his words.

evidence.note: FT report republished by Ars Technica on 2023-02-19, before the evaluation date. It names Pelrine as an amateur one level below the top amateur rank and says he won 14 of 15 games against a top-ranked Go AI (KataGo, per FAR AI).

reviews.rationale: Contemporary reporting confirms the claim: amateur Kellin Pelrine won 14 of 15 games against a top Go AI. The strategy came from computer-found exploits, but Marcus's post says so, and that does not change the score or the opponent's standing. No evidence in the packet points the other way.
